note: SPACE-001 protect source bytes: collection may delete what Jackage owns and never a user's source or uncommitted work, so src/space/source_protection.zig builds a subtractive plan - every candidate is checked against the protected roots and refused with a reason rather than collected. The plan deletes nothing; it is a description the caller performs, which keeps the safety decision auditable. Paths are normalized before the containment test, so a candidate written as cache/../../../../src/myproject/main.zig is recognized as source rather than trusted because its written form begins in the cache directory, and a path that escapes its root entirely is refused as not describing a managed location. Containment compares component boundaries, so a sibling directory sharing a prefix is not mistaken for source. My first test fixture was arithmetically wrong about how many .. components leave the jackage directory; the implementation was right and the fixture was corrected rather than the code. Fault proof: trusting the written path instead of normalizing it collects the disguised candidate and the refusal assertions fail (exit 1; the first fault attempt did not compile, which is a compile error and not a fault, and was retaken); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
authority: self-reported local review, not independent attestation
